common_name: HGC Jesko Hellebore (Gold Collection Large-Flowered White Christmas Rose)

planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in fall or early spring in rich, humus-laden, well-drained soil in partial shade; Jesko is a Gold Collection selection bred in Germany by Josef Heuger, propagated by division or tissue culture rather than seed.

directions: Set plants into humus-rich, evenly moist but well-drained soil in partial shade, mulching lightly to keep roots cool through summer. Jesko is a Gold Collection hellebore bred by Josef Heuger in Germany, prized for unusually large, rounded, pure white flowers 2-3 inches across with a central tuft of golden-yellow stamens; blooms open as early as late autumn in mild climates and continue into mid-spring, aging to a soft pale green as the stamens drop. The deep green, leathery, palmate evergreen foliage forms a tidy clump that stays attractive year-round. Remove old, tattered leaves in late winter just before flowering to best display the blooms, and divide congested clumps only occasionally, as hellebores resent frequent disturbance.

common_name: HGC Joel Hellebore (Gold Collection Early-Blooming White Christmas Rose)

planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in fall or early spring in rich, well-drained, humus-laden soil in partial shade; Joel is a Gold Collection selection bred in Germany by Josef Heuger, among the earliest Christmas roses to open, often flowering from December.

directions: Set divisions into rich, humus-amended, well-drained soil in partial shade, keeping soil evenly moist through the first season. Joel is a Gold Collection hellebore bred by Josef Heuger in Germany, notable for large white flowers borne on reddish leaf petioles and stems, which makes it a popular choice for winter cut-flower displays as well as garden use. Blooms open from December onward in mild winters, well ahead of typical Christmas rose timing. Deep green, leathery evergreen foliage persists year-round; cut back old, weathered leaves in late winter just before new flower stems emerge to keep the display clean.

common_name: HGC Jonas Hellebore (Gold Collection Star-Shaped Early White Christmas Rose)

planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in fall or early spring in rich, well-drained, humus-laden soil in partial shade; Jonas is a Gold Collection selection bred in Germany by Josef Heuger, flowering from November in mild climates.

directions: Set divisions into humus-rich, evenly moist but well-drained soil in partial shade. Jonas is a Gold Collection hellebore bred by Josef Heuger in Germany, bearing large, star-shaped, pure white flowers held on sturdy stems that can blush reddish in warm weather, above dense, fresh green evergreen foliage. It is one of the earliest-flowering niger selections, often opening from November onward well before the pre-Christmas season. Remove old, tattered leaves in late winter just before bloom to best showcase the flowers, and avoid disturbing the roots once a clump is established.

common_name: HGC Marlon Hellebore (Gold Collection Cream-to-Green Snow Rose)

planting.note: Transplant container-grown plants in fall or early spring into humus-rich, well-drained soil in partial shade, disturbing roots as little as possible; Marlon is a Gold Collection selection bred in Germany by Josef Heuger.

directions: Plant in well-drained but moisture-retentive soil enriched with compost, in partial shade beneath deciduous shrubs or trees that provide winter light and summer shade. Marlon is a Gold Collection hybrid (Helleborus niger x H. sternii) bred by Josef Heuger in Germany, opening blush-pink-tinted rose buds as early as November that unfurl into large, outward-facing cream flowers which gradually age to soft green as they mature. The leathery, evergreen, finely divided foliage provides structure through the year. Remove old, tattered leaves in late winter just before flowering to best display the blooms, and topdress annually with compost rather than dividing frequently.

common_name: Ice N' Roses Red Hellebore (Gold Collection Sterile Ruby-Red Snow Rose)
scientific_name: Helleborus x glandorfensis 'HGC Ice N' Roses Red'

planting.note: Transplant container-grown plants in fall or early spring into rich, sharply drained soil in partial shade; Ice N' Roses Red is a sterile Gold Collection hybrid bred in Germany by Josef Heuger, crossing Helleborus x ericsmithii with H. x hybridus.

directions: Good drainage is essential for best performance; plant in humus-rich soil that stays evenly moist but never waterlogged, in partial shade to light shade. Ice N' Roses Red is a Gold Collection hybrid bred by Josef Heuger in Germany, crossing Helleborus x ericsmithii with Lenten rose (H. x hybridus) to produce sturdy stalks of large, outward-facing, velvety ruby-red flowers over dark green, leathery evergreen foliage from late winter into spring. Because the cross is sterile, plants never set the abundant self-sown seedlings typical of Lenten rose, making it a lower-maintenance, long-lived clump former. Remove old foliage in late winter just before bloom to best display the flowers.

common_name: Harvington Hybrids Hellebore (Nunn Strain White Christmas Rose)

planting.note: Plant in fall or early spring in deeply cultivated, moist but well-drained, humus-enriched stony or alkaline soil in semi-shade, ideally against a wall or near an evergreen shrub; Harvington Hybrids is a vigorous, large-flowered seed strain developed by Liz and Hugh Nunn in Harvington, Worcestershire, UK.

directions: Plant in deeply worked, moist but fairly well-drained stony or alkaline soil enriched with humus, in semi-shade such as against a wall or beside an evergreen shrub; this strain is noted as not always easy to establish, so avoid disturbing roots once settled. Harvington Hybrids is a vigorous, large-flowered Helleborus niger strain developed over decades by Liz and Hugh Nunn, producing pure white, single, rounded flowers from January through April above semi-evergreen, deep green foliage. Remove old, faded flower stems after flowering, but leave the leaves intact unless seed is wanted, to encourage strong growth the following year.
